source.title: Tensor Programs V: Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer
source.authors: Greg Yang; J. Hu; Igor Babuschkin; S. Sidor; Xiaodong Liu; David Farhi; N. Ryder; J. Pachocki; Wei-Zhu Chen; Jian-Feng Gao

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training-loss results across widths, parameterizations, and hyperparameter settings, including CIFAR-10 MLP and ResNet experiments. These bear on whether width and training choices affect training outcomes, though its focus is hyperparameter transfer rather than the catalog’s exact zero-training-error claim.
record.gate_note: The text also discusses related results from prior work; those cited findings are not rows. Rows below are limited to this paper’s own CIFAR-10 training results. Validation-accuracy and language-model results are outside the claim versions’ stated training-error measures.
record.test_reason: The study tests hyperparameter transfer across model scales, which none of V1–V6 claims. Training-loss learning-rate sweeps do not establish near-zero training classification error, spurious local minima, depth degradation, initialization-dependent trainable depth, recovery above a measured stability threshold, or a batch-normalization advantage.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that µP makes hyperparameter landscapes reasonably stable across width, enabling tuning on smaller proxy models and zero-shot transfer to larger models. Transfer across depth, batch size, sequence length and training time has caveats, especially initialization-scale transfer across depth and post-layernorm depth transfer. Their wider-is-better observation is empirical and qualified by initialization and noise.
record.recipe_differences: The reported CIFAR-10 MLP experiment uses SGD and compares SP with µP over width and learning rate; the ResNet experiment uses SGD and transfers hyperparameters across widths. The paper studies hyperparameter-transfer behavior, not whether training classification error reaches zero.
record.method_sensitivity: For the MLPs, the learning-rate landscape changes with width under SP, while under µP the optimum is described as stable. CIFAR-10 ResNet validation performance also differs by parameterization and width.

fits_no_version.finding: For CIFAR-10 ReLU MLPs, SP's optimal learning rate shifts substantially across widths 256–8192; µP has a stable optimum and weakly improving performance with width at fixed learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: µP stabilizes training-loss hyperparameter optima across width in the tested MLP recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Transferring selected hyperparameters from width multiplier 0.5 to 8 gives Davidnet validation accuracy of 94.86% under SP and 95.29% under µP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: µP improves cross-width hyperparameter transfer for the tested CIFAR-10 Davidnet setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformer initialization-scale optima transfer less reliably across depth; depth transfer is fragile for post-layernorm Transformers. These concern hyperparameter transfer rather than plain-network trainable depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hyperparameter transfer across depth depends on the hyperparameter and Transformer normalization placement.

record.problems: The MLP training-loss results are shown in figures without tabulated exact values. For the ResNet experiment, the paper reports validation accuracy rather than training accuracy and says the model barely overfits; it gives no standard deviations for the table entries.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other reported studies and datasets are not included because their measures do not match the training-error behaviors named in the versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100; corrupted or random labels; smaller-model, early-stopping and regularization qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima frequencies and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons.
Plain-versus-residual convolutional depth degradation and its initialization or normalization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization preserving propagation across depth, resulting training speed and trainable depth, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian tanh training and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Loss recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability sharpness dynamics and divergence relative to measured thresholds.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable normalization-free Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdict is warranted. The authors' assertion that Davidnet validation trends also hold for training accuracy supplies neither training-error values nor evidence of near-zero error. Initialization sensitivity across width and activation blow-up during updates do not test V4's propagation and trainability claims across depth. Generic divergence does not test V5.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report zero or near-zero training classification error, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, or the stated smaller-model, early-stopping, and regularization comparisons.
No teacher-student ReLU problem, spurious local minima measurement, or student-versus-teacher neuron-count comparison.
No depth comparison of plain versus residual networks on training error, or test of shortcuts, very deep plain tanh training, or residual training without normalization.

The CIFAR-10 experiments compare parameterizations and width while sweeping learning rate; they do not test activation-matched initialization, vanishing or exploding signals and gradients, Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, or 10,000-layer plain convolutional training.
No learning-rate stability threshold, curvature, sharpness, or loss-catapult measurement.
No batch-normalization comparison or BN-associated speed and learning-rate tolerance test.

rows.subject: 2-hidden-layer MLP, width 256
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss across learning rates for CIFAR-10 MLPs under standard parametrization (SP).
rows.note: The figure plots the learning-rate sweep; no exact loss value is stated in text.
rows.check: Training cross-entropy for a shallow MLP does not measure V1's convolutional-network training classification error or any other version.

rows.subject: 2-hidden-layer MLP, width 256
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss across learning rates for CIFAR-10 MLPs under maximal update parametrization (µP).
rows.note: The figure plots the learning-rate sweep; no exact loss value is stated in text.
rows.check: The µP learning-rate landscape tests hyperparameter transfer, not any listed version; changing initialization and layer learning rates together does not isolate V4.

rows.subject: 2-hidden-layer MLP, width 8192
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss across learning rates for CIFAR-10 MLPs under standard parametrization (SP).
rows.note: Authors state that using the smallest model’s optimal learning rate on the largest gives very bad performance, if not divergence; this is not an exact zero-training-error result.
rows.check: Poor performance or divergence after transferring a learning rate does not test V5 without a stability threshold and recovery or curvature measurements.

rows.subject: 2-hidden-layer MLP, width 8192
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss across learning rates for CIFAR-10 MLPs under maximal update parametrization (µP).
rows.note: Authors state that the optimum learning rate is stable and performance for a fixed learning rate weakly improves with width; exact training error is not reported.
rows.check: Stable learning-rate optima across width do not establish near-zero training classification error or avoidance of spurious local minima.
